sph_dam_break_1d — DRIVE swarmflow op

• Data kinds: none → table (an op determined by its arguments alone — it takes no image or data input)

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.sph_dam_break_1d(h0: 'float' = 0.1, length: 'float' = 1.0, n_particles: 'int' = 400, t_end: 'float' = 0.2, g: 'float' = 9.81, kappa: 'float' = 1.3, alpha: 'float' = 0.3, n_out: 'int' = 5) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import swarmflow; swarmflow.sph_dam_break_1d(h0: 'float' = 0.1, length: 'float' = 1.0, n_particles: 'int' = 400, t_end: 'float' = 0.2, g: 'float' = 9.81, kappa: 'float' = 1.3, alpha: 'float' = 0.3, n_out: 'int' = 5) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("sph_dam_break_1d"))

• GPU: none (CPU reference implementation only)

Usage

Solves the dam break (dry bed) with 1-D SPH shallow-water equations (a model of the spreading when the swarm's gate is opened).

Water depth h_i = Σ_j m_j W(x_i − x_j, ℓ_ij) (1-D kernel, m = h₀ Δx), acceleration du_i/dt = −g Σ_j m_j ∂W_ij/∂x_i (= −g ∂h/∂x, in the symmetric form that conserves momentum) + Monaghan artificial viscosity. The smoothing length is per particle, ℓ_i = κ m/h_i (it widens where the front is thin), and pairs use the mean ℓ_ij. The left wall (x = −length) is represented by mirror particles. The ground truth is ritter_dam_break (compared by a gate).

Returns:

dict: t (K,), x (K, N), h (K, N), u (K, N) (particles at each time), front (K,) (the foremost particle),

mass (total mass, conserved), c0.
